headline: Good morning — and apologies for the hour: this AM edition fired about twelve hours late, so it is reaching you at dinner time in Bengaluru rather than breakfast. Here is what happened while it was asleep. The question Saturday's PM brief put to Frankie — resume the $300 Plan or leave it parked — was answered within six hours, and not by email. Frankie, you released Phase V2 at 1:00 PM your time Saturday: a new instant form with SMS OTP, state, age, an appointment-time picker and a required consent checkbox, on a $200 tranche across ten days. That is the most compliance-shaped thing this funnel has ever done, and it is worth saying so. The watchdog caught it ninety minutes later and has run every hour since — seventeen for seventeen — with every kill gate green: V2 spend is $56.06 of the $200, one lead so far, lifetime $261.45 and twenty-two leads. Now the one thing that actually matters today. That one V2 lead is real — an OTP-verified person who chose a time to be called — and it is sitting in Meta with no "NEW LEAD CAPTURED" email behind it. The last such email was September 2. The form-to-sheet-to-n8n-to-email path did not fire for the new form, and the watchdog has now said so for four hours running. Frankie: open Leads Center and pull that lead by hand today, and honor the time they picked. Chitraksh: the new form almost certainly has a new form ID that the capture webhook is not subscribed to — fix that path and prove it with one real submit before the next lead lands. Two smaller things behind that. The "honest broker" ad was not touched at release and very likely still uses the old form with no OTP; it has delivered nothing so far, but if it does, its leads skip every V2 gate — Frankie, one look in Ads Manager: confirm the form or pause it. And compliance: the consent checkbox is progress, but b3 and b7 are still open and five creatives went back live without the CA license number on them. Last: HQ has no written copy of the V2 plan — the $20-a-day you stated versus the $25 that is live, the ten days, the kill rules — this brief rebuilt all of it from the watchdog's emails. One paragraph in the workspace would let both founders and this brief read from the same page.
